content.text: The text reviews historical treatments for rectal prolapse, polyps, fistula, hemorrhoids, rectal hemorrhage, and nutrient enemas, then discusses intestinal parasites—especially tapeworms, flukes, nematodes, trichinae, and filariae—their life cycles, symptoms, treatments, and prevention through sanitation, filtration, and thoroughly cooked food. It then addresses liver disorders, including biliousness, lithaemia, glycosuria, jaundice, congestion, perihepatitis, cirrhosis, and hepatic abscess, emphasizing diet, historical medicines, diagnosis, complications, and surgical drainage.
